deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the existence part of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (Göttingen 1851), Arts. 16–18. The next page's table of contents labels Art. 15 as the minimum principle (Dirichlet principle) for Ω = ∫((∂α/∂x − ∂β/∂y)^2 + (∂α/∂y + ∂β/∂x)^2) dT. Here α is varied by functions λ that vanish on the boundary and are continuous except at isolated points.

(1) Uniqueness (top lines). Any two functions that make Ω minimal can differ only at isolated points. So once removable discontinuities are removed, the minimizer ω is completely determined.

(2) First variation. Let u = α + λ0 be the minimizer and λ an admissible variation (λ = 0 on the boundary). Expanding Ω(u + ελ) = Ω(u) + 2εN + ε²L shows that minimality forces
N = ∫∫ [ (u_x − β_y) λ_x + (u_y + β_x) λ_y ] dS = 0 for every λ.
Riemann states this and says further consequences are to be drawn from it.

(3) Integration by parts.
- Cut S into small pieces enclosing the discontinuities of u and β, plus the remainder S'.
- On S', apply the Gauss–Green theorem of Art. 7: ∫(∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT = −∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds, with p the inward normal.
- Take X = (u_x − β_y)λ and Y = (u_y + β_x)λ.
- [mine] Then ∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y = λ(u_xx + u_yy) + (u_x − β_y)λ_x + (u_y + β_x)λ_y, because the mixed β terms cancel (−β_yx + β_xy = 0).
- Hence the S'-part of N equals −∫ λ Δu dS − ∫ (∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) λ ds.
- [mine] The boundary density comes from (u_x − β_y)x_p + (u_y + β_x)y_p = u_p + (β_x y_p − β_y x_p), and the bracket equals ±β_s depending on the orientation convention linking s and p.
- Because of the boundary condition imposed on λ (λ = 0 on the outer boundary), the outer contour term vanishes. The contributions of the excised neighbourhoods are said to be negligible. N then reduces to −∫ λ Δu dS.
- [mine, implicit] Since λ is arbitrary, Δu = 0 away from the singular points.

(4) Consequence. Set X = u_x − β_y and Y = u_y + β_x. Then, generally speaking, ∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y = 0. Moreover, the flux ∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds over the whole boundary of any region in S vanishes (Art. 9).
- [mine, implicit; this is the continuation in the dissertation] Hence a single-valued ν exists with ν_x = −Y and ν_y = X, up to the sign convention.
- With v = β + ν, the pair u, v satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations, so u + iv is a function of z = x + iy.

(5) Admissibility condition (lower block). The discontinuities of u − α and v − β are restricted to isolated points. They are also restricted by the condition that the Dirichlet integrals ∫(((u−α)_x)^2 + ((u−α)_y)^2) dS and ∫(((v−β)_x)^2 + ((v−β)_y)^2) dS over the whole surface are finite.

(6) The last lines restart the paragraph: 'By Art. 15, for the function ω fixed there and every λ, N = ∫ over all of S = 0; from this equation further conclusions are to be drawn.'

The crossed-out heading 'Über die Unstetigkeiten einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Größe' (written upside down / repeated) is a discarded section title.
errors: Sign of the boundary term: with the convention on the next page (∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p, hence ∂y/∂s = −∂x/∂p), (u_x − β_y)x_p + (u_y + β_x)y_p = ∂u/∂p + ∂β/∂s, not ∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s. Riemann's minus sign is correct under the opposite orientation (∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s). This is a convention-dependent sign issue, possibly a slip or a change of convention between drafts; it is harmless because the term is killed by λ = 0 on the boundary.

The claim that the boundary contributions from the excised neighbourhoods of the discontinuities vanish is asserted without justification on this page. It requires the finite-Dirichlet-integral condition stated lower down.
The underlying existence of a minimizer (Dirichlet principle, Art. 15) is assumed. Weierstrass (1870) showed this step is not justified in general; it was later rescued by Hilbert (1900).
The line '∫(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) ds = 0' omits the factor λ that appears in the preceding formula. This is a slip of the pen or abbreviation.

results.what: Uniqueness of the minimizer of the Dirichlet-type functional Ω up to values at isolated points
results.modern_name: Uniqueness in the Dirichlet principle (strict convexity of the Dirichlet integral)

results.what: Vanishing first variation N = ∫(X λ_x + Y λ_y) dS = 0, integration by parts via Green's theorem, yielding Δu = 0
results.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange equation / Weyl-type weak formulation of the Laplace equation
results.usually_credited_to: Classical calculus of variations; in this setting Riemann 1851

results.what: Divergence-free field X, Y with vanishing flux on closed curves gives a conjugate function and hence an analytic u + iv
results.modern_name: Existence of the harmonic conjugate / Cauchy–Riemann completion (Dirichlet principle existence theorem)

results.what: Admissibility condition: singularities of u − α and v − β only at isolated points, with finite Dirichlet integrals

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the well-known Dirichlet-principle argument of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Arts. 16–18). The content matches the published text apart from wording and a convention-dependent sign, so it is of interest only for genesis and drafting history.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u,b,l=[Function(n)(x,y) for n in 'ubl']; X=(diff(u,x)-diff(b,y))*l; Y=(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))*l; simplify(diff(X,x)+diff(Y,y) - (l*(diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)) + (diff(u,x)-diff(b,y))*diff(l,x)+(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))*diff(l,y)))
checkable.asserts: Product-rule identity behind the integration by parts; the β terms cancel. Result should be 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u,b=[Function(n)(x,y) for n in 'ub']; simplify(diff(diff(u,x)-diff(b,y),x)+diff(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x),y) - (diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)))
checkable.asserts: div(X,Y) = Δu for X = u_x − β_y, Y = u_y + β_x. Result should be 0.

checkable.sympy: t=symbols('t'); a,c=cos(t),sin(t); xs,ys=a,c; xp,yp=-c,a; bx,by,ux,uy=symbols('bx by ux uy'); simplify((ux-by)*xp+(uy+bx)*yp - ((ux*xp+uy*yp) + (bx*xs+by*ys)))
checkable.asserts: With ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p (and ∂y/∂s = −∂x/∂p), the boundary density equals ∂u/∂p + ∂β/∂s. Result should be 0, confirming the sign remark.

checkable.sympy: t=symbols('t'); a,c=cos(t),sin(t); xs,ys=a,c; xp,yp=c,-a; bx,by,ux,uy=symbols('bx by ux uy'); simplify((ux-by)*xp+(uy+bx)*yp - ((ux*xp+uy*yp) - (bx*xs+by*ys)))
checkable.asserts: With the opposite convention ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s, the boundary density equals ∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s, matching Riemann's sign. Result should be 0.

transcription_corrections: 'Es können also gar die Functionen ω' should read 'Es können also zwei Functionen ω welche Ω einen Minimumwerth geben, nur in einzelnen Punkten von einander verschieden sein' ('gar' → 'zwei', 'und' → 'nur').
Insertion above 'Unstetigkeitsstellen' reads 'von u, β' (with 'Theil' at the right margin); the cut-off region is 'ein die Unstetigkeitsstellen von u, β umschließender Theil'.
'Wegschneidung von S' is probably 'Begrenzung von S' ('der von der Begrenzung von S herrührende Theil'), which fits the boundary-condition argument.
'u. l, durch die Bedingung beschränkt' should be 'auf einzelne Punkte und dadurch [durch die Bedingung] beschränkt' or similar; 'l' is not a variable.
In the first-variation formula, the crossed-out symbol before N is a false start ('λ, ...'), not part of the formula.
